name: What is the difference between Jacuzzi construction and Jacuzzi restoration?

mainEntity.name: When does a spa need full reconstruction versus repair or restoration?
mainEntity.text: When does a spa need full reconstruction versus repair or restoration?

acceptedAnswer.text: Jacuzzi construction and restoration solve different problems. Construction starts from scratch or creates a new built-in spa as part of a larger project. Restoration focuses on an existing spa that is worn, leaking, outdated, or no longer performing well. Restoration can include resurfacing, replacing pumps or heaters, repairing plumbing, updating tile, or improving the surrounding deck. In some cases, a spa is so damaged or poorly built that rebuilding is more economical than patching. The decision usually depends on the condition of the shell, structure, plumbing, and equipment. Homeowners should ask for an inspection that separates cosmetic issues from structural ones. If the spa has chronic leaks, cracked support, or outdated systems, a full rebuild may be the smarter long-term choice. If the shell and layout are sound, restoration can provide a strong return without starting over.
acceptedAnswer.description: Construction builds a new Jacuzzi from the ground up, while restoration repairs or upgrades an existing spa. Restoration may include resurfacing, equipment replacement, tile repair, or updated plumbing, but it does not usually involve full site redesign.
